column6: Cambridge bullet said "the Cambridge School reads single texts as moves in immediate debates" but Pocock tracked political languages over long periods; narrowed to Skinner. Also trimmed unverified clause "the same concept can appear under more than one word" from the concept/word bullet (not counted wrong).
Absolute "All societies use the past to define themselves" softened to "Societies routinely".
Explainer attributed "the past is a foreign country" to "the philosopher"; it is the opening line of L. P. Hartley's novel The Go-Between. Corrected attribution.
Note (not fixed): older Common Misconceptions section runs two bullets onto one line and lacks the "(correction)" format.
Bullet said emplotment "also covers" plain sequencing; in White's sense emplotment is specifically the plot-type encoding. Added qualifier that the wider sense is Ricoeur's usage.
Explainer said the phrase "history from below" "comes from the socialist press tradition" (unsupported); replaced with its popularization by E.P. Thompson's 1966 TLS essay "History from Below".
Explainer sat before Questions; moved Explainer after the Questions block to match the required section order. Text unchanged.
Note (old text, not fixed): Q1 explanation calls the "normal exception" Ginzburg's key move; the phrase (eccezionale normale) is Edoardo Grendi's, later used by Ginzburg and Poni.
